faqs.q: What award covers a contracts administrator salary?
faqs.a: There is no single award for all contracts administrators. The correct award depends on the industry. For example, a contracts administrator in the contract call centre industry may be covered by the Contract Call Centres Award [MA000023], while one in property services may fall under the Property Industry Award. Check the Fair Work Ombudsman's list of pay guides or use the Pay and Conditions Tool to find the award that applies to your role.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to a contracts administrator salary?
faqs.a: If you are a casual employee, the award usually requires a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. For example, if the base rate is $30.00 per hour, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour. This loading is included in the hourly rate you enter into the timesheet calculator. The annual and fortnightly figures shown on this page assume the base rate without casual loading unless stated otherwise.

faqs.q: Does the super guarantee apply to a contracts administrator salary?
faqs.a: Yes. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee is 12% of ordinary time earnings, paid on top of your gross salary. For a contracts administrator earning $69,160 per year, the employer would contribute an additional $8,299.20 in super, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This super is not included in the take-home pay figures.

bodyMarkdown:
## Contracts Administrator Salary: From Hourly to Annual

If you work as a contracts administrator, you might be paid by the hour or offered an annual salary. Understanding how to convert between the two helps you compare job offers and plan your finances. This guide uses a standard 38-hour week and a 52-week year, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman, to show you the annual, fortnightly, and weekly equivalents of your hourly rate.

### The Basic Formula

To convert an hourly rate to an annual salary, multiply the hourly rate by the number of hours worked per week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time contracts administrator working 38 hours per week:

**Annual gross salary = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

For example, if your hourly rate is $35.00:
- Annual gross = $35.00 × 38 × 52 = $69,160
- Weekly gross = $35.00 × 38 = $1,330
- Fortnightly gross = $1,330 × 2 = $2,660

This formula assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It is a starting point for estimating your pay.

### National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. A casual employee receives at least $33.05 per hour, which includes the 25% casual loading. However, most contracts administrators are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides [pay guides](/blog) for each award, listing the minimum hourly rates, allowances, and penalty rates. Use the Pay and Conditions Tool to find the award that applies to your role.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. Knowing your fortnightly gross amount helps with budgeting. Using the same $35.00 per hour example, your fortnightly gross is $2,660. After tax and Medicare, your take-home pay will be lower. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page can help you estimate your net income.

### Tax on Your Contracts Administrator Salary

For the 2026–27 financial year, the Australian Taxation Office resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (based on 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a $69,160 annual salary, the estimated tax and Medicare would be approximately $11,217, leaving a take-home of about $57,943 per year. This is an estimate only; use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool for a more detailed calculation.

### Superannuation Paid on Top

Your employer must pay super guarantee of 12% of your ordinary time earnings, on top of your gross salary. For a $69,160 salary, that is an extra $8,299.20 per year, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This super is not deducted from your pay; it is paid separately into your super fund. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Comparing Job Offers

When you receive a job offer as a contracts administrator, compare the total package including super. A salary of $75,000 per year plus 12% super is worth $84,000 in total remuneration. If you are paid hourly, multiply your rate by 38 × 52 to get the annual equivalent. The [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page shows that full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026 (Australian Bureau of Statistics), which is about $108,352 per year. Your contracts administrator salary may be above or below this average depending on experience and industry.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

On [the timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; the calculator will apply it correctly. The calculator then shows your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross amounts, plus estimated tax and super.

### Important Assumptions

This guide assumes a 38-hour week and 52-week year. It does not account for unpaid leave, overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, and tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. The Medicare levy uses 2025–26 single reduction thresholds. HELP repayments, Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. Always consult the [reference tables](/data) for the latest rates.

### Summary

To convert a contracts administrator salary from hourly to annual, use the formula hourly rate × 38 × 52. For a rate of $35.00 per hour, that is $69,160 per year. Your fortnightly gross is $2,660. After tax and Medicare, your take-home is lower, and super is paid on top. Check the Fair Work Ombudsman's [pay guides](/blog) for your award's minimum rates, and use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for the latest national minimum wage.
